thread:
omar: Quick sync — I'm rethinking the ingest <-> prober adapter boundary. We're seeing 3 recurrent problems: (1) full bench runs block admission for 30+ mins, (2) warmup/kv-cache expectations differ between runtime and prober, and (3) adapters have inconsistent retry semantics.

lina: Totally. My instinct is to formalize two lanes: 'quick-probe' (fast smoke + basic KV warmup) and 'full-bench' (longer, golden coverage + quantization checks). quick-probe should be the default for CI/onboard PRs.

tj: +1 to lanes. We need a minimal handshake schema so the ingest gateway and runtime know what to expect. Suggested fields: probe_lane, expected_warmup_tokens, quantization_tolerance. Without that, runtime falls back inconsistently.

omar: Example minimal contract I sketched:

```
adapter_handshake:
  probe_lane: "quick"  # quick | full
  max_seq: 256
  warmup_tokens: 128
  require_kv_warm: true
  allow_quantized_variants: false
```

maya: That looks reasonable. For quick-probe do we agree on sample size? I'm thinking 40-60 short prompts drawn from stratified buckets (nouns, code, multi-turn) so we catch tokenization regressions.

raj: Concern: quick-probe will not catch stateful failure modes like KV eviction patterns or off-by-one in cached attention indices. Those only show up in long sequence replay. If we default everyone to quick, we're risking silent regressions. :thinking_face:

lina: Mitigation: require a periodic full-bench run before model is promoted to stable (e.g., 1 successful full-bench within 24h). For Dedicated/Private customers we gate promotion on full-bench. For hosted dev flow, a calendar-triggered full-bench is fine.

tj: Metrics to track for lane gating: pass_rate, p95_latency, sample_error_rate (token-level mismatches vs baseline). Pass threshold ideas: quick-probe >= 99.5% and full-bench >= 99.95% with golden divergence < 0.2%.

omar: Operationally, implement these as separate job kinds in the intake service. quick-probe runs inline with ingest (give short timeout), full-bench is scheduled to bench fleet and returns a summary report. Proposal: quick returns "fast_ok" | "fast_flag"; full returns detailed verdict with artifacts.

maya: Small UX suggestion for triage: quick-probe failures should include 3 representative examples and a pointer to the full-bench artifact id. That makes oncall's life easier.

raj: About retry semantics — adapters currently retry differing numbers of times on transient inference errors. We should standardize: adapters do at most 2 retries with exponential backoff, but full-bench uses no retries (we want raw failure surface).

omar: Good call. Also thinking about a light-weight prober CLI to let SEs run quick-probe locally:

```
rwi prober run --model-id rwi-123 --lane quick --samples 50 --seed 17
```

lina: Love that. One more boundary Q: who owns golden sample curation? bench team or model owners? We should centralize curation in bench team but allow owners to propose additions. Ownership clarity avoids drift.

tj: Agreed. Add a metadata field to handshake: golden_set_id so the runner knows which golden to compare to.

omar: Final strawman next steps: 1) land adapter_handshake schema in ingest repo, 2) implement quick vs full lanes in prober orchestrator, 3) add a promotion gate requiring at least one full-bench for stable tag, 4) docs + CLI. I'll open an RFC PR today.

bench-bot: scheduled: full-bench rwi-123 in bench-fleet (ETA 2h) — will post artifact id when done. :robot_face:

maya: Thanks — can we also add a smoke for quantized runtime differences? Full-bench should include low-precision run and compare token divergence.

omar: Yup — include quant checks in full lane. I'll call out acceptance thresholds in the PR. If no objections I'll start the PR now. :shipit:
